subject: science
domain: Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions
skillName: Testing a Push or Pull Design

items.prompt:
The results we observe from a test are called
A) data
B) colors
C) names
D) sounds

steps: Data are the observed results of a test.

items.prompt:
A ramp meant to make a ball faster does make it faster. The design
A) worked
B) did not work
C) has no goal
D) broke

steps: The ball did what was intended, so it worked.

items.prompt:
A wall meant to change a ball's direction makes it turn. The design
A) worked
B) failed
C) did nothing
D) made it stop forever

steps: The ball changed direction as intended.

items.prompt:
A ramp was meant to speed up a ball, but the ball went the same speed. The design
A) worked
B) did not work as intended
C) was perfect
D) made the ball slower on purpose
items.answer: B) did not work as intended

steps: The ball did not go faster, so it failed the goal.

items.prompt:
We look at data after a test to
A) see if the design worked as intended
B) change the color
C) make noise
D) nothing
items.answer: A) see if the design worked as intended

steps: Data tell us whether the design did what we wanted.

items.prompt:
If a design did not work, you should
A) change it and test again
B) give up forever
C) ignore the data
D) break it
items.answer: A) change it and test again

steps: You can improve and retest the design.

items.prompt:
A steeper ramp makes a ball go faster than a flat ramp. The data show that
A) the flat ramp is faster
B) the steeper ramp speeds the ball up more
C) ramps do nothing
D) the ball never moves
items.answer: B) the steeper ramp speeds the ball up more

steps: The data show the steeper ramp works better for speed.

items.prompt:
The BEST way to tell if a ramp sped up a ball is to
A) guess
B) compare the ball's speed on flat ground and on the ramp
C) look at the ball's color
D) weigh the ramp
items.answer: B) compare the ball's speed on flat ground and on the ramp

steps: Comparing the speeds is the data that shows if it worked.
